name: Oregon Health & Science University

profile.address: 505, Northwest 185th Avenue, Amberglen, Beaverton, Washington County, Oregon, 97006
profile.reading:
This facility in Washington County, Oregon is attributed to Oregon Health and Science University (OHSU), the state's academic health center and largest hospital based research and teaching institution, headquartered on Marquam Hill in Portland. The building sits in the Amberglen area of Beaverton, along Northwest 185th Avenue, inside a technology and office corridor that also hosts networking, semiconductor and corporate campuses associated with the broader Silicon Forest cluster west of Portland.

OHSU is not a commercial data center operator. Like most large academic medical centers, it runs its own enterprise IT infrastructure to support electronic health records, clinical imaging, research computing and administrative systems across its hospital, clinic and university campuses. Locating that infrastructure away from the main Marquam Hill hospital complex is a common resiliency practice among health systems, since a facility physically separated from the primary campus reduces the chance that a single incident, such as a fire, flood or power outage, disrupts both patient care operations and the systems that support them.

OHSU previously operated a satellite campus in Washington County through the former Oregon Graduate Institute (OGI), which it absorbed in 2001 and largely vacated by 2014 when those programs relocated to Marquam Hill. Public sources describe that transition in general terms but do not establish whether this particular Washington County data center descends from the OGI era footprint or is a separate facility built or leased specifically for enterprise IT use. Either origin would be consistent with a university and hospital system owned facility rather than a colocation or cloud provider site, and neither points to a commercial tenant.

Because OHSU treats this building as internal infrastructure supporting protected health information and research systems, it does not publish power capacity, square footage, tier rating or tenancy details for it, and no county permit or property record specific to this address has surfaced in the sourcing behind this entry. That silence is itself informative: hospital systems generally decline to publicize the location or specifications of data centers holding clinical and research data, for security and regulatory reasons, not because nothing is there. The entry will be updated if verifiable capacity, ownership or facility detail becomes publicly available.
